prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: Round 1 showed that all six of us arrive at the same configuration, and I again treat that as a reason to check the argument, not as the argument. The scientific case holds on re-examination. Incretin physiology and proglucagon processing (Holst), receptor biology and the intestinotropic and metabolic actions (Drucker), and the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov) form a discovery chain that explains why degradation-resistant agonists work. Independent large trials have confirmed the effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, so maturity is not in doubt. The discovery is describable in one sentence, and a single-part prize keeps the credit within three names. My answer to the chair's question on a second part is no. The GLP-1 part already uses all three slots, and none of B039, B036, B018 or B004 has a configuration I find cleaner than the GLP-1 trio. I would not dilute a well-supported part to add one with an open attribution problem.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and round 1 did not remove it. Mojsov's priority for the active truncated peptide is contested, and I am relying on recollection, as several of you are, because the supplied material does not settle it. Habener is outside the credit list and cannot be added by us. Knudsen, who led liraglutide and semaglutide, is outside the three-name cap. I have considered whether to substitute Knudsen for Mojsov. Her work is the development step, and Holst and Drucker already carry the physiology and therapeutic rationale. Replacing a discovery scientist with a developer would change the prize from a discovery prize into a development prize, and I cannot justify removing Mojsov on evidence I cannot verify. If the committee found that Mojsov's priority could not be defended, I would prefer a Holst and Drucker pair to a swap, and I would want that decision made on documents, not memory.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius said Holst and Drucker are secure under any resolution of the priority question, that Knudsen would be the strongest replacement if Mojsov cannot be defended, and that she sees no principled way to remove Holst or Drucker to make room for the drugs.
responses.response: I agree that Holst and Drucker are the fixed points, and that nobody could reasonably drop either to reach Knudsen. Where I differ slightly is on the fallback. If Mojsov's claim fails, I would first test a Holst and Drucker pair, as El-Manira suggests, before bringing Knudsen in, because the substitution changes the nature of the prize from physiology to development. I accept your point that Knudsen's claim becomes the strongest if a third name is still wanted. I do not think the evidence in front of us justifies triggering that fallback now. I also accept your view that a separate part or a different year is the principled route for the development work.

responses.point: Perlmann proposed keeping the discovery trio, reflecting the therapeutic consequence through citation wording, and named Habener and Bell as early proglucagon contributors outside the list, while also raising B039 and B004 as possible second parts.
responses.response: I agree with the discovery trio and with using the citation to show the clinical consequence, which is why my wording says the discoveries enabled the therapies. Your point about Habener and Bell matters for the narrative, and I accept that no configuration within our cap is fully clean. I still do not support a second part. On TOR, our views differ. I would keep a Hall and Schreiber core, and the clinical benefit beyond transplantation and a few cancers is narrower than the biology. On B039, I take your concern about solid tumours, toxicity and manufacturing as a maturity difference from incretin therapy, and that supports keeping GLP-1 alone this year. I would add that my collaboration with you is disclosed and does not bear on any credited name.

responses.point: El-Manira proposed that the committee test a Holst and Drucker pair before deciding on the third name, and judged that long-term durability of the obesity benefit does not change the case.
responses.response: I support the test you propose. I would ask whether the Holst and Drucker pair fully describes the discovery, and my answer is that it describes the physiology but leaves out the identification of the active peptide, which is the step that links secretion to the agonists. That is why I keep Mojsov in the preferred configuration while recording the priority doubt. I also agree on durability. Weight regain after stopping and long-term safety are open questions about the treatment, but they do not alter that the mechanism is established and that effects on glycaemia and cardiorenal outcomes are well documented.

responses.point: Linnarsson accepts a June and Sadelain pair for CAR-T and says a prize paired with GLP-1 makes the three-person cap costly, while flagging Eshhar's absence as a fairness problem.
responses.response: We agree that Rosenberg's work is adoptive cell therapy more broadly than the CAR, and that Eshhar's absence is the heavier problem for B039. That is why I keep B039 as my first alternative and not as a second part. If GLP-1 were not available, I would want June and Sadelain with a citation that is careful about the chimeric receptor concept. Pairing it with GLP-1 would require dropping a GLP-1 name or leaving out Eshhar, and I do not see a fair version of either.

responses.point: Sandberg called Mojsov the weakest link in the trio but kept her, and said a two-part prize would dilute the credited names, which she currently thinks is not worth it.
responses.response: I agree that Mojsov is the weakest link, and I agree on the two-part question. Your uncertainty about whether her priority is secure enough is my own. My position is that the record we can see does not give a documented reason to remove her, and removing her on recollection would be an unfair act in itself. I disagree with nothing in your reading of durability. I treat safety and durability as characterisation of the drugs and not as a challenge to the discovery.

uncertainties: Whether the active-peptide priority between Mojsov and other groups can be settled from documents. I still rely on recollection, and my position depends on that gap not being closed against her.

Whether the committee should recognise the development work of Knudsen within a prize or leave it to the narrative. I lean toward the narrative, but I could be moved if the committee sees the prize as one for the medicine.
Habener's and Bell's early contributions are outside the supplied credit list, and I cannot say how they should affect the allocation among the three named laureates.
Whether B039 is better as June and Sadelain or with Rosenberg, and how Eshhar's absence should be handled, which matters only if it becomes the primary choice.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. My profile records about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy (count not independently audited), and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. I see no connection to Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen or any other credited name on the shortlist, so I do not think recusal is required, and I record the Perlmann collaboration as disclosed. No new conflict arose in round 1.
